comments.note: gui/public/js/api.js uses ES module syntax (export) but package.json does not declare "type": "module". Node emits a MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON warning when the file is imported directly in tests. Adding "type": "module" to package.json would suppress the warning, but this has wider implications (all .js files in the project would become modules) so it should be a deliberate decision rather than a drive-by fix.

There are no GUI-side (api.js) tests in the existing test suite. The new api.errorLog.test.mjs establishes a pattern for testing the GUI API client. The other namespaces (repositories, projects, workspaces, branches, status, config) have no unit tests at all — future WPs could follow the same pattern to add coverage.

The JSDoc @type block on the export const api object (lines 522-534) documents namespace types inline. When errorLog is used by view code, IDE tooling will correctly resolve api.errorLog.* method signatures because the namespace const is hoisted above the export. The pattern is consistent with all other namespaces.

comments.note: Edge case verified: list({}) (empty params object) does not append a query string — the Object.keys().length > 0 guard handles this correctly.
Edge case verified: list() with params containing only undefined values correctly emits no query parameters due to the per-key !== undefined guards.
MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON warning appears during test execution (non-fatal). Pre-existing issue noted by Developer; no impact on correctness.
No sanitization of the id parameter in get(id) — consistent with all other namespaces in api.js. Not a defect, but callers must validate IDs before use.

comments.note: api.js line 457 (errorLog.get): Changed `/api/error-log/${id}` to `/api/error-log/${encodeURIComponent(id)}` for consistency with all other namespaces (repositories.get, projects.get, workspaces.get, config.credentials.delete, etc. all use encodeURIComponent on path segments). For a numeric id this is behaviorally identical (encodeURIComponent(42) === '42'), but aligns with the file's established convention and guards against future type widening to string.

[documentation-forward] The api.errorLog namespace (api.js lines 424-478) should be documented in the project's API client reference. Specifically: document the list() filter params shape ({ severity?, source?, limit?, offset? }), the count() badge-counting pattern (GET /api/error-log?limit=0), and the clear() 204 → undefined contract. Any existing API client guide or README section covering api.* namespaces should be updated to include errorLog.

[documentation-forward] The new test file gui/public/js/api.errorLog.test.mjs establishes the first GUI-side unit test pattern for the api.js client. Consider documenting how to run GUI-layer tests in the project's contributing guide or test documentation, since this pattern did not exist before this WP.

list() has a slightly over-defensive double-guard: the outer Object.keys(params).length > 0 check is redundant given each key individually checks !== undefined, and the inner if (qsString) guard handles the empty-params case anyway. No bug — logic is correct — but a future refactor could simplify to a single qs-building pass without the outer length check.
